general_background.title: Indium carboxylate as a precursor
general_background.summary: Indium acetate can be exchanged into a more soluble indium carboxylate by a long-chain acid before a phosphorus reagent is added. Conversion of the carboxylate and the formation of intermediate clusters can separate precursor consumption from the emergence of larger crystals.

general_background.title: Saturated carboxylic acids can supply coordinating carboxylate
general_background.summary: Stearic acid can make a long-chain metal carboxylate when it reacts with a metal oxide or exchanges with a shorter ligand. Both the identity of the soluble feed and carboxylate binding at the surface can affect colloidal growth.

general_background.title: Stable cluster intermediates can delay particle growth
general_background.summary: In some indium phosphide routes, unusually stable molecular clusters accumulate instead of turning immediately into a smoothly growing distribution. Their appearance breaks the simple link between mixing the precursor and forming the final nanocrystals.
